subject: Feathered cutover deployment — detailed orchestration & rollback playbook
messages:
From: Priya Sengupta <priya.sengupta@aurorafin.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Philip Jensen <pjensen@aurorafin.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: RFP follow-up — implementation sequencing, telemetry & rollback detail request

Vanessa,

Thanks for the RFP response — Aurora's implementation committee wants a more granular walk-through on how Redwood would execute a production cutover for our API traffic. Specifically:

- A phased timeline (weeks/days) with gating criteria for each stage.
- Integration touchpoints (auth, event/webhook mapping, schema compatibility).
- Canary/feathered routing mechanics and the telemetry thresholds that trigger hold/rollback.
- Expected downtime or user-visible impact for each workstream (DB sync, model switchover, DNS).
- Contingency and rollback runbook steps (including fast-fail and staged rollback).

Can you provide a technical playbook and a short summary we can present to the committee on Nov 22? We may have minor procurement asks after that.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Sengupta
Head of Platform Integrations
Aurora Financial

Attachment: — none —
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sengupta <priya.sengupta@aurorafin.com>, Philip Jensen <pjensen@aurorafin.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — implementation sequencing, telemetry & rollback detail request

Priya / Philip —

Appreciate the clear asks. Ive attached a draft playbook weve prepared for Aurora: Redwood_Feathered_Cutover_Playbook_v1.pdf. High-level summary for the committee:

1) Timeline (recommended):
   - Week 0 (Prep): configuration sync, IAM mapping, test account provisioning.
   - Week 1 (Stage): non-prod integration verification, schema compatibility checks, contract tests.
   - Week 2 (Feathered Canary): 1% live traffic to Redwood, telemetry collection, prefix/KV cache warm-up.
   - Week 3 (Stepped Ramp): 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 48–72 hours with clear hold criteria.
   - Week 4 (Full cut): route 100% with rollback window for 24 hours.

2) Integration touchpoints: OAuth/OIDC token exchange, mutual TLS option, webhook retry semantics, response schema validation (we provide a sample adapter).

3) Telemetry & gating (see Feathered_Canary_Telemetry_Matrix.xlsx):
   - Error rate > 0.5% 5-min rolling OR token latency P95 increase > 35% = HOLD.
   - Throughput drop > 20% or downstream error propagation triggers immediate rollback.

4) Rollback playbook:
   - Fast-fail: toggle traffic back to incumbent via edge route control (sub-second).
   - Staged rollback: reverse the last ramp step (e.g., 50% -> 20% -> 5% -> 0%) if telemetry degrades but system is stable for degraded gradual rollback.
   - Post-mortem requirements: time-stamped traces, call-stack samples, and request sample set for evaluation.

Im copying Markus (runtime lead) and Laura (solutions architect) to align on technical gating thresholds and the artifacts youll need for procurement.

Attachments: Redwood_Feathered_Cutover_Playbook_v1.pdf; Feathered_Canary_Telemetry_Matrix.xlsx; MAOP_Traffic_Thresholds.csv

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0196
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Feathered cutover deployment — detailed orchestration & rollback playbook

Vanessa — forwarding Priya's questions and your draft. A few internal notes and requested edits before we send to Aurora: 

On Thu, Nov 17, 2026 at 11:43 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Priya / Philip —
> 
> Appreciate the clear asks. Ive attached a draft playbook weve prepared for Aurora...

Internal items (actionable):
- Telemetry thresholds: raise the error-rate HOLD from 0.5% -> 0.75% for high-volume endpoints (we should include endpoint-level vs global).
- Add a specific DB-sync step: we recommend a dual-write + verification window for 48 hours for Aurora's transactional profile. Nail down the exact verification query (suggest sample SQL in appendix).
- Clarify DNS expectations: we will use route-level edge steering (no DNS TTL flips required), but include vendor contact if Aurora insists on BGP level cutover.
- Legal/Procurement ask: include a 2-week rollback SLA in the contract appendix for any config-level regressions. Coordinate with Laura for exact language.

Laura — can you draft the verification SQL + consumer contract test vector? Also please produce a short bulletsheet (1 page) Aurora can present to their committee.

— Markus

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Priya Sengupta <priya.sengupta@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Philip Jensen <pjensen@aurorafin.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Feathered cutover deployment — detailed orchestration & rollback playbook

Priya / Philip —

Thanks for the patience. Updated artifacts attached and a short committee-friendly bulletsheet below (also uploaded to the Drive link):

Committee bulletsheet (1 page):
- Objective: Zero-customer-impact migration to Redwood inference with measurable rollback triggers.
- Recommended cadence: 4-week feathered cutover (Prep, Stage, Feathered Canary, Ramp, Full).
- Key safety nets: duplicate writes for 48h, route-level edge steering for sub-second fallback, cold-start cache prefetch for critical prefixes.
- Telemetry gates (examples): endpoint-level error rate >= 0.75% over 5m; latency P95 increase >= 40% vs baseline; downstream queue length growth > 2x baseline.
- Rollback options: (1) Immediate edge toggle. (2) Progressive unwind of ramp steps. (3) Emergency halt + fallback to incumbent for critical customers.
- Procurement/Legal ask: 14-day rollback support SLA; trace-level export for post-mortem.

Technical appendix highlights (attachments):
- Verification SQL: SELECT COUNT(1) FROM transactions WHERE redwood_flag = TRUE AND processed_ts > NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'; compare with legacy counts; tolerance +/- 0.5%
- Consumer contract test vector: sample request + expected response (schema + 5 example payloads).
- Telemetry matrix: mapping of metric -> window -> threshold -> action.

Next steps: Vanessa — please send the committee bulletsheet + the updated playbook link. Markus — if you agree with the threshold tweaks Ill add the exact language to the playbook appendix.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0132
